title: Models for three timing families rarely had complete weather inputs three months before their reference month
abstract: We audited 26,103 climate-response model series from two signed studies. Training ended in 2004 and later tests used mainly 2005-2024. We checked whether each selected weather window was complete at a fixed issue time. Among models with training cross-validated R2 of at least 0.10, only 34 of 2,069 German spring models, 2 of 108 Japanese cherry models and no lake or river ice models had complete inputs three months before reference month-end. Their full-set median later skills with observed weather were 0.38, 0.50 and 0.45 against a trailing mean. Only 5, 1 and 0 models had both complete inputs and later skill above 0.05. US river flow differed: 268 of 635 models had complete inputs and 255 had skill above 0.05. A rule that switches to the trailing mean when inputs are incomplete can be scored exactly from the published statistics. The result survives two training signal screens. This exploratory audit measures the availability of drivers in fixed fits. It does not test archived weather forecasts or new fits with earlier windows. Reference months are not actual event dates. Reporting delays and revised inputs can further limit use. Code, exact input hashes, aggregate evidence and an independent count check are included.

display.caption: Complete driver coverage at a three-month deadline, and coverage with later skill above 0.05 across deadlines. Primary training screen: R2_cv >= 0.10. Reference months differ across families.

citations.reason: Published model-statistic table supplies selected weather windows and later forecast scores. We audit issue-time availability; raw source records are not used.
